why: The founder's ruling of 28 October 2026, item 6: any sentence, Why? text or rationale that says or implies a cloud provider documents a behaviour carries the page's URL, the exact sentence quoted and the date read. The kit takes the shape of arvaken/mark's check (mark#914). A claim cites its entries by id, [source: id], in the README or in a comment or docstring, never in words a customer is shown. tests/test_provider_claims_name_their_source.py fails the build on a claim with no source.

fields.url: the page, https, on the provider's own host
fields.sentence: the sentence (or list, table row or entry) quoted whole, no ellipsis
fields.about: what the sentence is about, in the provider's own terms
fields.read: the day it was read, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC)

google-storage-403-forbidden.sentence: forbidden: This error can occur for several reasons: According to access control policy, the current user does not have access to perform the requested action, and this can occur even if the resource being acted on doesn't exist; or the request is missing the overrideUnlockedRetention query parameter but is attempting to change an object's existing retention configuration in a way that requires the parameter; or the request is attempting to change a locked object's retention configuration in a way that requires the object to be unlocked.

google-storage-401-auth-error.page: HTTP status and error codes for JSON | Cloud Storage | Google Cloud Documentation
google-storage-401-auth-error.sentence: authError: This error indicates a problem with the authorization provided in the request to Cloud Storage. The following are some situations where that will occur: The OAuth access token has expired and needs to be refreshed. This can be avoided by refreshing the access token early, but code can also catch this error, refresh the token and retry automatically. Multiple non-matching authorizations were provided; choose one mode only. The OAuth access token's bound project does not match the project associated with the provided developer key. The Authorization header was of an unrecognized format or uses an unsupported credential type.
google-storage-401-auth-error.about: the 401 Unauthorized reason authError, an expired access token among its situations
